SRC-300:R012.text: Maintainability problems with demonstrated engineering cost. Every proposed ticket must include: - Exact file and symbol. - Reproducible defect or measured opportunity. - Evidence of why it matters. - Expected engineering benefit. - Scope and compatibility boundary. - Minimal proposed change. - Acceptance criteria. - Regression risks. - Verification method. - Existing related ticket, if any. - Estimated test and execution cost. Deduplicate by root cause before admission. Do not accept a proposal supported only by generic language such as "clean this up", "improve code quality" or "optimize architecture". WORKSTREAM C — TEST EXECUTION COST REDUCTION The user specifically wants the excessive cost of test execution reduced without loss of safety. Relevant modules: tools/saipen_engine/test_runner.py tools/saipen_engine/verification_cache.py tools/saipen_engine/conformance.py tools/saipen_engine/continue_loop.py First establish a reproducible baseline: - Total wall-clock validation time. - Python test collection time. - Number of executed test cases. - Per-family execution cost. - Slowest tests and setup fixtures. - Number of repeated equivalent test runs. - Cache hit/miss rate. - Time spent validating unchanged source. - Time spent on canonical conformance checks. - Time spent on packaging and installation checks. - Time spent on serial work that is safely parallelizable. Then investigate: C01. Redundant setup and teardown. C02. Repeated full suites after unrelated changes. C03. Incorrect cache invalidation. C04. Excessive subprocess initialization. C05. Filesystem and Git scans repeated with identical inputs. C06. Path identity and environment identity instability. C07. Test fixtures rebuilding unchanged resources. C08. Unnecessarily serial independent tests. C09. Repeated expensive protocol validation. C10. Slow or flaky tests caused by timeouts and polling. C11. Excessive log serialization and evidence processing. C12. Opportunities for deterministic impact-based test selection. Build a safe validation strategy: FAST: focused red-to-green tests for the changed root cause. IMPACTED: related tests selected through trustworthy dependency information. FULL: required authoritative regression gates at meaningful acceptance boundaries. Do not use FAST success to claim FULL success. Never reuse stale verification receipts. Never suppress a failing test merely to improve runtime. Measure before and after. Reject optimizations that trade correctness for artificial speed. WORKSTREAM D — RECURSIVE CODE AND PROTOCOL SIMPLIFICATION Perform targeted analysis of: tools/saipen.py tools/saipen_engine/router.py tools/saipen_engine/board.py tools/saipen_engine/operations.py tools/saipen_engine/goal_authority.py tools/saipen_engine/continue_loop.py tools/saipen_engine/conformance.py tools/saipen_engine/audit_inbox.py Look for verified instances of: D01. Duplicated decision logic. D02. Multiple incompatible implementations of the same rule. D03. Repeated parsing and serialization. D04. Overlapping fallback branches. D05. Expensive compatibility paths no longer used. D06. Unreachable code with proof of unreachability. D07. Obsolete adapters that can be retired safely. D08. Inconsistent typed error/status contracts. D09. Unnecessary filesystem writes. D10. Excessive work during read-only commands. D11. State transitions that can produce ambiguous outcomes. D12. Error recovery that repeats an already-failed operation indefinitely. D13. Documentation that conflicts with the executable contract. D14. Hidden dependencies between installation and repository runtime. Apply only changes with demonstrable benefit. Preserve backward compatibility where required. Prefer one shared mechanism over accumulating additional wrappers and fallback layers. Never rewrite large subsystems just because they appear complicated. WORKSTREAM E — STAGING AND BLOCKER SAFETY Investigate whether T-1815 can make safe progress without altering the operator's foreign staged batch. Requirements: E01. Inspect exact live index ownership and Git state. E02. Determine whether canonical isolated verification or an isolated worktree can safely separate the authorized implementation from foreign staged changes. E03. Preserve the original index byte-for-byte when ownership is not established. E04. Do not silently move or unstage another actor's files. E05. Do not force-push, rewrite branch history or publish without the established publication authority. E06. Never fabricate a release receipt to unblock a dependent ticket. E07. Where safely isolated work is possible, continue its independent implementation and verification. E08. Where publication requires the operator's decision, retain the blocker and work on other improvements. E09. Provide a precise blocked-root summary rather than asking the user to inspect the entire backlog. WORKSTREAM F — CONTINUOUS LIVENESS Implement a low-overhead, host-controlled continuation strategy. The persistent controller must not depend on repeatedly asking a human to type cc. The controller may resume only work for which the current authority is valid. If independent executable work exists: Execute the highest-value authorized task. If no executable task exists but useful engineering evidence exists: Perform bounded improvement discovery and implementation. If discovery produces no new actionable findings: Enter QUIESCENT_IDLE. QUIESCENT_IDLE means: - No endless LLM calls on unchanged inputs. - No meaningless ticket creation. - No repeated full test suites without changed evidence. - No fake progress. - No busy polling. - Preserve checkpoints and all unfinished work. - Wake automatically on a legitimate new task, relevant source change, recovered external dependency or an appropriately spaced maintenance interval. Do not claim that idle polling itself constitutes progress. Where the host supports an authorized scheduler, use a durable scheduled or event-driven wakeup. Preserve resource and process isolation. If the host cannot provide continuous execution, report the missing host capability precisely rather than pretending that a chat session can guarantee 24/7 execution. WORKSTREAM G — CRASH, AUTHORITY AND SAFETY G01. Reuse the existing persistent goal authority framework. G02. A verified persistent goal crosses its ordinary ticket checkpoint automatically. G03. An ordinary bounded goal still respects its hard_wait boundary. G04. A new objective or expanded scope requires appropriate authority. G05. Source receipts and journal history survive restart. G06. No model-generated text may impersonate a native operator event. G07. An active foreign execution seat cannot be stolen. G08. External publication remains independently gated. G09. Protected staging remains untouched. G10. Failed tests never become successful through status rewriting. G11. Recovery must be idempotent. G12. Repeated failures must generate one durable incident record rather than an infinite retry loop. G13. Maintenance work must be preemptible by newly admitted higher-priority user work. G14. Checkpoint and cancellation must leave the repository recoverable. G15. An improvement that introduces regression must be reverted or repaired before proceeding to unrelated changes. WORKSTREAM H — ACCEPTANCE MATRIX H01. DONE state with no DOING or executable TODO enters an authorized maintenance campaign. H02. Ordinary goal mode without maintenance authority retains its existing STOP behavior. H03. A genuine operator-authorized maintenance mission can resume after restart. H04. Existing active improvement cycles resume rather than duplicate. H05. An unchanged source does not trigger endless identical audit cycles. H06. Previously unexamined high-value surfaces can still be audited with distinct scope and evidence. H07. All 106 blocked tickets remain correctly classified unless their actual blockers are resolved. H08. T-1815 and the 206 foreign staged paths remain protected. H09. A valid persistent goal crosses 20, 21, 28, 50 and 100 processed-ticket checkpoints without redundant human authorization. H10. A bounded unauthorized goal still stops correctly. H11. A genuine new user task preempts lower-priority maintenance at a safe checkpoint. H12. A crash during ticket selection does not create duplicates. H13. A crash during verification does not fabricate PASS. H14. No source change and no useful findings result in low-cost QUIESCENT_IDLE. H15. Relevant source changes reactivate the controller. H16. An external blocker does not block independent authorized improvement. H17. Performance improvements include before/after measurements. H18. Refactoring preserves regression contracts. H19. Installation and deployed runtime parity remain valid. H20. Publication remains subject to the existing authenticated policy. H21. A 12-hour simulated or real controlled campaign does not accumulate duplicate work, stale authority or runaway resources. H22. The controller reports actual completed engineering changes, not uptime as its main KPI. IMPLEMENTATION ORDER P0: - Preserve existing active work and blockers. - Establish a new authorized maintenance mission. - Implement safe goal-to-maintenance routing. - Complete the improvement-cycle lifecycle. - Provide recovery and idempotency tests. P1: - Measure and reduce test execution cost. - Improve expensive routing and validation paths. - Eliminate reproducible duplicated logic. - Complete genuine root-cause regression repairs. P2: - Simplify documentation and protocol projections. - Improve diagnostic efficiency. - Reduce unnecessary filesystem activity. - Consolidate redundant internal mechanisms. P3: - Lower-priority readability and maintainability improvements only when evidence shows value. ANTI-BUSYWORK POLICY Do not: - Create tickets to increase the completed-ticket count. - Re-run identical audits without fresh scope or evidence. - Count a prepared improvement cycle as completed engineering work. - Perform broad rewrites without a measured reason. - Reformat large codebases merely to show activity. - Delete historical evidence for cosmetic cleanliness. - Trade test coverage for speed. - Hide external blockers behind an idle-maintenance label. - Make unauthorized changes outside SAIPEN. - Keep a model generating tokens solely to satisfy a 24/7 activity requirement. METRICS Record per campaign: - Verified defects discovered. - Verified defects repaired. - Regressions prevented. - Test execution time before/after. - CPU time and I/O saved. - Duplicate mechanisms actually eliminated. - Lines or modules removed where justified. - New recurring test failures. - Recovery success rate. - Number of unnecessary operator interventions. - Idle resource consumption. - Remaining independent executable work. Do not use ticket count or lines changed as standalone measures of productivity. FINAL EXECUTION CONTRACT Continue autonomously while authorized, useful executable work remains. Prefer verified engineering benefit over broad speculative cleanup. After each completed slice:

SRC-300:R017.text: Continue with the next useful slice. If all actionable engineering opportunities have been exhausted, transition to QUIESCENT_IDLE with automatic supported wakeups, not a fake perpetual work loop. If an actual human-controlled decision is unavoidable, preserve that exact boundary and continue unrelated authorized work. The intended result is a continuously available SAIPEN engineering system, not an indefinitely spinning agent. SUCCESS DEFINITION An empty ordinary task queue no longer needlessly ends an authorized maintenance mission. SAIPEN continuously finds and completes measurable improvements when such improvements exist. When no valuable action exists, it waits efficiently and resumes automatically when justified. No security regression, no fabricated authority, no lost tasks, no empty work generation, no hidden manual continuation requirement.
